label: History
value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby lived in a home situated at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley.
unit: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby lived in a home situated at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, sitting by her window to watch everyone passing along the main road. One June afternoon, she spotted Obed Abernethy driving out of Brierley dressed in fine clothes, which ruined her peace until she visited Grey Shutters to learn from Thirza that Obed had gone to collect an orphan boy. Upon learning the next day that a red-haired orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, arrived instead due to a mix-up, Mrs. Agatha expressed strong disapproval. Weeks later, after recovering from a bout of influenza, Mrs. Agatha visited Grey Shutters to inspect Nell and made blunt remarks calling her plain, thin, freckled, and red-headed, provoking Nell into a fiery rage. When Nell later visited her home to deliver a dramatic, remorseful apology, Mrs. Agatha readily forgave her, offered her hope about her hair, and gave her white June lilies. Over the following years, Mrs. Agatha remained an active presence in Brierley, participating in political rallies, Aid Society meetings, and community events. She eventually admitted she was wrong in her initial harsh assessment of Nell, acknowledging that the girl had grown into an attractive and clever young lady.

label: History
value: Nell is sent from the Marden asylum to Brierley by mistake
unit: Sent by mistake from the Marden asylum to Brierley instead of a boy, Nell is brought to Grey Shutters by Obed Abernethy. Though initially unwanted by Thirza Abernethy due to her gender and loquacious nature, Nell's imagination and charm win over both Obed and Thirza, who decide to keep her. She quickly makes Grey Shutters her beloved home, forms a close friendship with Isolde Pembroke, and begins attending Brierley School under Mr. Pidgeon. Despite early mishaps—such as a fiery outburst at Agatha Sowerby, accidentally getting Isolde drunk on currant wine, and accidentally dyeing her hair green—Nell settles into community life and excels academically. In a fierce academic rivalry with Hugh Carrow, Nell works tirelessly under her beloved teacher Miss Thorne, ultimately passing the Entrance Exam and winning the prestigious Avery Scholarship to Wexcombe College. However, after Obed dies of a sudden heart attack and Thirza's eyesight threatens to fail, Nell selflessly forfeits her scholarship to remain at Grey Shutters. She accepts the teaching position at Brierley School—yielded to her by Hugh Carrow—reconciles with Hugh, and commits herself to caring for Thirza and their home.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters
unit: Obed Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters in Brierley alongside his sister, Thirza. Struggling with advancing age, heart trouble, and difficulty securing hired labor, Obed persuaded Thirza to adopt a young boy from an orphanage in Nova Scotia to assist on the farm. Traveling to Alder River station to collect the child, he discovered an eleven-year-old orphan girl named Nell Harcourt instead of a boy due to a mix-up. Fearing to break the news immediately to the eager girl, he brought her back to Grey Shutters. Though Thirza initially insisted on returning Nell, Obed took a liking to her loquacious nature and quietly advocated for keeping her. Throughout Nell's upbringing, Obed consistently doted on her, buying her treats and supporting her desires, such as persuading Thirza to let her go to a local concert and purchasing a stylish puffed-sleeve dress for her. When the Abbey Bank unexpectedly failed, wiping out all of their savings, the sudden shock triggered a fatal heart attack, and Obed passed away in the porch doorway of his home.
